problems.title: Directional maps are assigned by head rather than query group
claim: The paper defines four query-token groups, but reshaped attention is \((B,H,Q,K)\) and the source chunks dimension \(1\), the head axis.
analysis: For production \(H=12,Q=16,K=273\), each directional chunk contains three heads and all sixteen queries. At the first spatial key, head \(0\), query \(4\) receives left coefficient \(1\), though query \(4\) belongs to the right group and needs \(0\). Head \(3\), query \(0\) receives right coefficient \(0\), though the left group needs \(1\). Every query within a head shares the same map. Downstream injection treats the resulting token groups as directional keys; no inspected deterministic head-to-token map supplies the missing query grouping.
result: The source mask does not implement the declared query-group routing. Learned queries may still specialize and relighting may improve; no same-defect claim is made for FLUX.
repair: For the documented design, broadcast \(G_{bhqk}=m_{\lfloor4q/Q\rfloor}(k)\), with \(Q\) divisible by \(4\), along the query axis. This changes the architecture and requires checkpoint/quality evaluation.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local implementation or interpretation defect; damage to the central empirical result has not been established.

problems.title: A zero spatial coefficient can favor a negative logit
claim: The release multiplies raw dot-product scores by maps in \([0,1]\), then softmaxes them.
analysis: Two keys with equal logits \(-2\) and left/right coefficients \((1,0)\) become \((-2,0)\); conditional pair shares are \[0.1192029220,0.8807970780\], rather than equal shares before masking. The supposedly removed right key has odds \(e^2\) times the left. These are valid dot products, for example \(q=(1,0,0,0)\), both keys \((-4,0,0,0)\), head width \(4\). The pair odds hold inside the full \(273\)-key row and are not claimed as full-row probabilities. Positive logits can favor the intended side and zero logits are unaffected.
result: The unconditional attenuation interpretation fails on legal signed scores. No actual PSNR/FID or trained-token counterexample is established.
repair: For an unnormalized probability gate, compute \(A=\operatorname{softmax}(L)\), then \(\widetilde A=A\odot G\), with no second softmax. This gives \(0\le\widetilde A\le A\) and preserves coefficient-one special keys. A separately normalized gate equals softmax of \(L+\log G\), but changes absolute special-key weights and must be described as a different choice.
